title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). The base field k is algebraically closed of characteristic not 2. J is the 3-element set of nonzero 2-torsion points of E, and V_J = Ker(k^J -> k, sum) is a plane. Sigma_J = P^1(V_J) is the projective line of lines in V_J, with three marked points eps_i = k(e_j - e_k). Sigma_J^* is Sigma_J minus these three points. In modern terms Sigma_J^* is an intrinsic, J-equivariant model of the lambda-line, i.e. the coarse space of Y(2). A point t is a line F_t in V_J. The line t_E is the tangent line (Lie algebra) of E. The isomorphism nu: t_E^{(x)2} ~ T_{Sigma_J,t} is the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism.

What this page does.

(62) It makes the tangent line explicit. T_{P(V),t} = Hom(F_t, V/F_t). Using V/F_t ~ F_t^dual (x) Lambda^2 V, this gives T ~ O_t(2)(omega), where O_t(1) = F_t^dual ~ V/F_t (twisted by omega). Here omega (underlined) is the determinant line Lambda^2 V_J, which is canonically Lambda^3 k^J. It comes equipped with the pair of generators +-e_1^e_2^e_3; the two signs correspond to the two cyclic orders of J (the 'two circular roots'). Because omega^{(x)2} is canonically trivial, twisting by omega or by omega^{-1} is the same.

(63) Kodaira-Spencer therefore becomes nu: t^{(x)2} ~ F_t^{(x)-2}(omega). Its dual form is t^{(x)-2} ~ F_t^{(x)2}(omega). So the basic data of a level-2 elliptic curve are (J, F_t in V_J, t_E, nu).

(64)-(66) Grothendieck then defines a 'Legendre pinning' (epinglage de Legendre). It is a family of isomorphisms kappa_i: t_E ~ O_t(1) = F_t^dual(omega), indexed by the two primitive 4th roots of unity i in mu_4^*, with the rule kappa_{1/i} = i kappa_i. Equivalently, on duals, kappa^_{1/i} = (1/i) kappa^_i.

(67) The compatibility condition says that kappa_i^{(x)2} equals nu followed by wedging with a chosen generator omega_i of the line omega.

What this encodes. Concretely, kappa_i is a choice of invariant differential (the Legendre dx/y) normalised against the lambda-coordinate. The appearance of mu_4^* reflects the sign/quadratic-twist ambiguity of Legendre normal form: y^2 = x(x-1)(x-lambda) and its -1-twist become identified only after adjoining sqrt(-1). On the next page, the consequence omega_{i'} = -omega_i yields a bijection alpha: mu_4^* ~ omega, i.e. it links a choice of i to a cyclic orientation of J. Overall this is a coordinate-free account of the Legendre family over the lambda-line, aimed at a modular (moduli-stack) description of Legendre pinnings over Z[1/2, i].
errors: No mathematical error found. The identity T_{P(V),t} ~ F^dual(x)V/F ~ F^{dual (x)2}(x)Lambda^2V is correct.
The sign consistency holds: kappa_{1/i}^{(x)2} = i^2 kappa_i^{(x)2} = -kappa_i^{(x)2}, which forces omega_{1/i} = -omega_i, as stated on the next page.

Minor notational slips: (67) writes t^{(x)2} where underlined t is meant. (67) also drops the twist (omega) in the target, where F^{(x)(-2)}(omega) is meant before wedging with omega_i. The 'nu_Sigma' in the text should read nu_E.

ideas.what: Intrinsic description of the lambda-line as P(Ker(k^J -> k)) with three marked points, functorial in the 3-set J of nonzero 2-torsion points
ideas.modern_name: Modular curve X(2) = P^1 with cusps; S_3-equivariant model of Y(2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi); modern stack version Deligne-Rapoport 1973, Katz-Mazur 1985
ideas.where_published: Thematically close to the role of P^1 minus 3 points in Esquisse d'un programme, but this explicit construction is not published there

ideas.what: Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism t_E^{(x)2} ~ T_{Sigma,t} written as O(2) twisted by the determinant line omega_J
ideas.modern_name: Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism omega^{(x)2} ~ Omega^1(log cusps) on modular curves

ideas.what: Legendre pinning: mu_4^*-indexed trivialisations kappa_i of t_E compatible with Kodaira-Spencer, giving a bijection between primitive 4th roots of unity and the two orientations (circular roots) of J
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification of the Legendre family (choice of differential dx/y) over Z[1/2, i]; quadratic-twist ambiguity of Legendre form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Katz-Mazur and in treatments of the Legendre family (Igusa, Deuring)

missed.claim: This is a fully intrinsic, J-functorial formulation of Legendre normal form. The Legendre differential is tied to a bijection mu_4^* ~ {orientations of J}, with no coordinates chosen. Such a coordinate-free account of why sqrt(-1) enters the Legendre pinning is not standard in textbooks. It is an expository refinement, however, not a new theorem.
missed.quote: kappa_{i'} = i kappa_i si i' = 1/i est l'autre élément de mu_4^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal value for clean S_3-equivariant treatments of the Legendre/lambda-line stack and its descent from Z[1/2, i] to Z[1/2]. The underlying mathematics is known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful, canonical bookkeeping of known facts: Kodaira-Spencer on the lambda-line and the sqrt(-1) ambiguity of Legendre form. The orientation/mu_4 bijection is a nice intrinsic touch, but it is not a new result.
transcription_corrections: (64) 'O_t(1)^4' most likely denotes a mu_4^*-indexed family (see (65)), not a 4th tensor power.
'nu_Sigma s'interprète' should probably read nu_E (or nu).
(66) the source of kappa^_i is the dual line (t-check), as in 'kappa^_i : t^ ~ F_t(omega)'.
(62) 'O_t(1) ~ V_J/F_t ~ F^_t(omega)' — the twist is by the underlined omega (the determinant line), consistent with (63).
Last line: 'bien déterminé par kappa, i, en fait par kappa_i'. The transcription reads 'ou fait'; the image reads 'en fait'.
